label: D-10 job-seeking status: maximum total period of stay
appliesTo: General job-seeking (D-10) holders looking for work in E-1 to E-7 fields
why: It changed in October 2025 and a great deal of published guidance did not. University pages and forum answers still describe the old six-month grants to a two-year ceiling, so a graduate planning a job search from those sources budgets a year less than they actually have. This is the clearest case on the site for why a figure needs a recorded history rather than a current value.

history.source: Ministry of Justice — general job-seeking (D-10) rules as they stood before the 2025 reform
history.note: The position immediately before the reform: granted in six-month periods to a cumulative ceiling of two years. Recorded because guidance describing it is still in wide circulation.

history.source: Ministry of Justice — reform of the general job-seeking (D-10) system, effective 29 October 2025
history.note: Up to one year per grant, to a cumulative ceiling of three years. The eligibility conditions were not removed by the reform: the degree requirement, the job-seeking field and the points test are all still assessed separately.
